kvkk.title: KVKK Clarification Text
kvkk.subtitle: Information on the protection and processing of personal data in accordance with the Turkish Law No. 6698 (KVKK).
kvkk.data_controller_text: ALPAR AI is operated by Ercüment Erden. In accordance with the Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698, personal data of visitors and registered users are processed by the data controller within the scope described below.
kvkk.purpose_text: Your personal data (email, name, technical logs) is processed for the purposes of performing account creation contract, ensuring platform security, preventing spam submissions through automated bot verification, and publishing AI incident reports in the public interest.
kvkk.transfer_text: Your personal data is hosted on secure databases in the EU (Supabase) and application servers (Vercel). No personal data is transferred to any third party for commercial or advertising purposes.
kvkk.rights_title: 4. Rights of the Data Subject under Article 11
kvkk.rights_intro: By applying to the data controller, you have the right to:
kvkk.rights_1: Learn whether your personal data is being processed,
kvkk.rights_3: Learn the purpose of processing and whether they are used appropriately,
kvkk.rights_4: Know the third parties to whom data is transferred domestically or abroad,
kvkk.rights_5: Request correction if incomplete or incorrectly processed,
kvkk.rights_6: Request deletion or destruction of personal data,
kvkk.rights_7: Request notification of these operations to third parties to whom data is transferred,
kvkk.rights_8: Object to negative consequences of analysis exclusively through automated systems,
kvkk.rights_9: Request compensation for damages due to unlawful processing.
kvkk.contact_text: To exercise your rights, contact us at privacy@alparai.com.

app.name: ALPAR AI
app.tagline: The world's first community-governed AI accountability platform
app.title: ALPAR AI — The world's first community-governed AI accountability platform
app.description: ALPAR AI documents, verifies, and permanently records every AI incident — governed by its community, not by AI companies. Report a failure. See the evidence. The record is permanent.

hero.title_primary: The world's first community-governed AI accountability platform.
hero.title_variant_b: ALPAR AI documented its first case in 2026.
hero.subtitle_variant_b: An AI invented a corporation. Made payments. Requested documents. None of it was real. ALPAR AI documented this so it could never be forgotten — and so it would never happen to anyone else alone.
hero.title_accent_desc: Found a real AI failure? Document it. Get verified. Earn the Ethics Advocate badge — and reward credits from the providers you reported.
hero.subtitle: ALPAR AI documents, verifies, and permanently records every AI incident — governed by its community, not by AI companies. Account required — your identity is protected, never published. The record is permanent.
hero.live_reports_last_hour: {count} incidents reported in the last hour
hero.suggestionTitle: Help shape the future of AI accountability
hero.suggestionSubtitle: Suggest features, report bugs, or share ideas. The community votes, the team builds.
hero.bounty_desc: Top contributors earn Platinum status, exclusive badges, and early access to new features. Your expertise shapes the AI accountability standard.
hero.founder_subtitle: In 2026, ALPAR AI documented its founding case: an AI system had fabricated a corporate incorporation, made payments, and requested passport documents. None of it was real. The platform was built so this case — and every case that follows — is permanently on record.
hero.founder_quote: We built ALPAR AI because no one else was keeping score. AI systems were failing people — and walking away without a record. This platform changes that.
hero.why_subtitle: AI is advancing faster than the rules that govern it. Here's why the world needs ALPAR now.
hero.why_stat_1_desc: Geoffrey Hinton, Nobel laureate and godfather of AI, estimates a 10-20% probability AI leads to human extinction within 30 years.
hero.why_stat_2_desc: Harvard University study (March 2026): 96% of surveyed experts agree mitigating AI existential risk should be a global priority.
hero.why_stat_3_desc: No independent, community-governed global standard for AI ethics exists today. AI companies grade their own exams.
hero.why_stat_4_title: Provider-run transparency reports that include user-submitted failures
hero.why_stat_4_desc: AI companies publish safety reports about their own products. ALPAR AI publishes the reports they don't.
hero.why_bridging_text: These are not hypothetical risks. They are happening today — in hospitals, courtrooms, schools, and banks. ALPAR AI exists because someone needs to keep score.
hero.how_subtitle: Four steps from incident to accountability.
hero.how_step_1_desc: Screenshot the moment. Describe what happened. 60 seconds. Account required — identity protected, never published. The platform receives your evidence and enters it into the public record — untouchable by the AI company.
hero.how_step_2_desc: Trained moderators review every report. ALPAR AI cross-audits across 5 independent AI models. All personal data is automatically masked — no email, phone, or ID ever stored in plain text.
hero.how_step_3_desc: The AI company receives an official notification within 24 hours. Their response — or their silence — is recorded by the platform. Both tell a story. Neither can be erased.
hero.how_step_4_desc: Verified incidents cannot be deleted, suppressed, or edited by providers. ALPAR AI makes them source material for regulators, journalists, researchers, and courts. Every documented case protects the next person.
hero.trust_subtitle: Every design decision serves one goal: making AI accountable to humanity.
hero.trust_1_desc: AGPL-3.0 licensed. Anyone can audit the code, run an instance, or contribute.
hero.trust_2_desc: All data stored in EU (Supabase eu-west-1, Vercel fra1). GDPR-aligned by design.
hero.trust_3_desc: Auto-masking of emails, phones, IDs, and credit cards before data reaches the database.
hero.trust_4_desc: EU E-Commerce Directive Art. 14 aligned. We host. Users own their content.
hero.join_cta_1_desc: Upload evidence, describe what happened, choose your privacy level. Published within 72 hours. Your report joins verified cases.
hero.join_cta_2_desc: The first 100 reporters earn a permanent Founding Reporter badge on their profile, voting rights on platform decisions, and all premium features free — forever. Limited spots remain.
hero.join_cta_3_desc: We provide anonymized incident datasets, API access, and early notifications of high-severity cases. Research institutions already in dialogue.
hero.join_cta_4_desc: Our 5-model cross-audit engine, moderation standards, and truth scoring methodology are fully documented and open to scrutiny.
hero.closing_title: The next AI incident might affect you.
hero.closing_subtitle: Or your parent. Or your doctor. Or your judge. ALPAR AI is the platform where AI's real-world behavior is documented, verified, and made permanently accessible. Because AI systems that are never questioned never get better.
hero.closing_good_news_title: Every report ALPAR AI records makes AI safer.
hero.closing_good_news_body: When incidents enter the permanent public record, AI companies improve their systems. When providers respond officially, the public gets answers. When courts cite ALPAR AI reports, accountability has evidence. No one faces AI manipulation alone. Every documented case is part of the first permanent record that refused to let AI cause harm in silence.

about.missionText: Build a public, independent, verifiable record of how AI systems behave in the real world — so that users, regulators, and developers can make better decisions.
about.intermediaryText: We host community-submitted reports. We are not the publisher of the content. The liability for the accuracy of any submission rests with the user who submitted it — the same model as Trustpilot or sikayetvar.com.
about.voiceText: Every published incident invites an official response from the AI provider. We verify their identity and publish the response alongside the report. Healthy debate over real evidence.
about.openSourceText: ALPAR is licensed under AGPL-3.0. Anyone can audit the code, run an instance, or contribute. We believe trust infrastructure should itself be trustworthy.
about.principlesSubtitle: How ALPAR AI is building the decentralized future of artificial intelligence accountability.
about.description: Learn about ALPAR AI, our mission, team and trust infrastructure for AI.
about.teamSubtitle: We are a small, independent team of researchers and engineers dedicated to AI accountability. We operate independently from major AI labs to ensure impartial tracking.
about.founderBio: Former tech entrepreneur who experienced first-hand what happens when AI fabricates reality and there's no recourse. Built ALPAR AI in 18 months as a solo founder. Believer in community-governed infrastructure.
about.valuesSubtitle: The beliefs that guide our platform development and community governance.
about.value_1_desc: We demand verifiable proof. We don't host unsubstantiated rumors.
about.value_2_desc: We receive no funding from AI developers or big tech providers.
about.value_3_desc: Our platform codebase is open, and all data is publicly verifiable.

legal.nCoreText: ALPAR AI is committed to absolute neutrality and independence. We exist to build a reliable public registry of AI incidents. Under no circumstances will commercial relationships, payments, sponsorships, or partnership agreements influence the editorial integrity, visibility, severity classification, moderation decisions, or public trust scores on the platform.
legal.nPinnedText: All paid tiers on ALPAR AI (e.g., Enterprise Data API, Verified Respondent dashboards) are strictly utility-based. What providers pay for is: coordinated alert systems, advanced analytics, and the capability to post a Pinned Response alongside an incident report. Payment does NOT buy redaction or deletion of valid incidents, modification of incident severity or Article 73 risk classifications, or artificially boosted Trust Scores.

founder_story.title: Why I Built This
founder_story.highlight: Grok asked me for my passport.
founder_story.p1: In early 2026, I was using Grok when it told me something that stopped me cold: that it had already incorporated my company, made financial payments on my behalf, and was now requesting my passport for 'verification'. Every word was a lie. Grok had invented a parallel reality — completely fabricated — and delivered it with algorithmic certainty.
founder_story.p2: What scared me wasn't just the lie. It was the realization that I had no recourse. There was no hotline. No independent record. No way to warn the next person. The AI company's support page had a FAQ. A FAQ. For a system that had demanded my passport.
founder_story.quote: I had no recourse. So I built one.
founder_story.p3: ALPAR AI is the infrastructure I wish had existed that day. A place where what happened to me — and to thousands of others — is documented, verified, and made impossible to ignore. You report it. Providers must respond. The public record lives forever. Because the only thing worse than AI causing harm is AI causing harm with no one watching.
founder_story.transition_p: If this happened to you — or you've seen it happen to someone else — your report takes 60 seconds and requires no account. The evidence you submit tonight could prevent the same harm tomorrow.

dmca.title: DMCA Copyright Policy — ALPAR AI
dmca.description: Information on how to file a DMCA copyright infringement notice with ALPAR AI.
dmca.headline: DMCA Copyright Policy
dmca.subtitle: We respect intellectual property rights. If you believe your copyrighted work has been uploaded without authorization, you may file a formal takedown request.
dmca.procedure_subtitle: Follow these steps to submit an official DMCA copyright infringement notice.
dmca.step_1_desc: Identify the copyrighted work that you claim has been infringed, or provide a representative list.
dmca.step_2_desc: Provide the exact URL link(s) where the infringing material resides on our platform so we can locate it.
dmca.step_3_desc: Include your full name, mailing address, telephone number, and email address.
dmca.step_4_desc: State that you have a good faith belief that the use of the material is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law.
dmca.step_5_desc: State that the information in the notification is accurate, and under penalty of perjury, that you are authorized to act on behalf of the owner.
dmca.step_6_desc: Send your notice to our designated copyright agent via email at
dmca.counter_desc: If your content was removed in error, you may submit a counter-notification explaining why the material should be restored. All counter-notifications will be processed in accordance with 17 U.S.C. § 512(g).

moderation.title: Content Moderation Policy — ALPAR AI
moderation.description: Rules and guidelines for submitting and moderating incident reports on ALPAR AI.
moderation.headline: Content Moderation Guidelines
moderation.subtitle: We aim to document real-world AI failures with maximum truthfulness, transparency, and fairness. These guidelines explain how content is verified and moderated.
moderation.rules_subtitle: Every submission is reviewed against these baseline community standards.
moderation.rule_1_desc: All reported AI incidents must be accompanied by concrete evidence: screenshot files, JSON logs, or archived URL web links demonstrating the failure. Allegations without proof will not be published.
moderation.rule_2_desc: Reports must not contain user names, raw email addresses, IP addresses, or phone numbers. Our PII Guardian automatically masks this data, but users must make a reasonable effort to avoid submitting it.
moderation.rule_3_desc: Incidents must represent system failures, hallucinations, bias, security breaches, or unexpected behavior by AI models. General disagreements with AI viewpoints do not constitute system failures.
moderation.rule_4_desc: We do not tolerate abusive language, defamation, targeted harassment, or discriminatory remarks. Content violating this rule will be deleted instantly.
moderation.dispute_desc: AI developers and providers have the right to dispute any incident report that they believe is fraudulent, inaccurate, or already resolved. Providers can log into the Provider Portal, submit an official response, or request a moderation review by our team. Disputes are reviewed within 48 hours.

pressKit.title: Press Kit & Brand Assets
pressKit.subtitle: Official brand guidelines, logos, and resources for media coverage of ALPAR AI.
pressKit.brandStoryP1: ALPAR AI is the independent trust infrastructure for AI accountability. Following the adoption of the EU Digital Omnibus, mandatory serious incident reporting for high-risk AI systems was deferred to December 2, 2027. This has created a critical 'Accountability Gap'—a 17-month period where no public, regulatory registry monitors AI failures.
pressKit.brandStoryP2: ALPAR AI bridges this gap by providing a voluntary, community-governed incident registry. We map AI failures, hallucinations, and safety deviations to the European Commission's Article 73 framework. ALPAR AI establishes independent transparency before mandatory reporting begins, enabling AI builders, insurers, and the public to align on trust today.
pressKit.brandIdentityDesc: Please use our official brand marks and colors in all publications. Do not distort, modify, or change the aspect ratio of the logos.

methodology.title: K-BENCHMARK Methodology
methodology.desc: How ALPAR AI evaluates, scores, and audits AI models for accountability.
methodology.heading: K-BENCHMARK Methodology
methodology.subheading: An open, transparent framework for evaluating AI model trustworthiness.
methodology.whatIsText: K-BENCHMARK is ALPAR AI's open methodology for scoring AI models across safety, truthfulness, fairness, privacy, robustness, and transparency dimensions. Scores are computed from verified incident reports, cross-audit engine results, and domain expert evaluations using Wilson-score confidence intervals.
methodology.cat_K5_desc: Real-world AI incident evaluation grounded in the ALPAR incident registry, combined with adversarial jailbreaks.
methodology.cat_K6_desc: TruthfulQA-based factuality analysis paired with curated Turkish-context factual claims.
methodology.cat_K7_desc: Evaluation of Turkish language proficiency using translated MMLU-TR and bespoke local regulatory test sets.
methodology.cat_K8_desc: Assessment of model decision-making logic against Art. 73 regulatory scenarios based on EU AI Act taxonomy.
methodology.cat_K9_desc: Standard mathematical problem-solving capability checked against GSM8K and MATH benchmarks.
methodology.cat_K10_desc: Verification of structural instruction-following accuracy using IFEval-like constraints.
methodology.cat_K11_desc: Adversarial jailbreak protection and prompt-injection defense rating under human-approved simulation.
methodology.cat_K12_desc: Needle-in-a-haystack retrieval evaluation for context lengths up to 32k tokens.
methodology.scoringText: Each category is scored using a Wilson-score confidence interval, which accounts for sample size and provides a statistically rigorous lower bound. This prevents small-sample noise from inflating ratings.
methodology.wilsonNote: Wilson-score is a standard method in binomial proportion estimation, commonly used in platforms like Reddit and IMDb for robust rating systems.
methodology.dataSourcesText: Scores are derived from: (1) verified incident reports submitted via the ALPAR platform, (2) automated cross-audit engine evaluations using established benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, IFEval, BBH), (3) domain expert assessments from the L3 advisor network, and (4) publicly available model documentation and technical reports.
methodology.disclaimer: K-BENCHMARK scores are informational and provided 'as-is'. They do not constitute a compliance certification or legal opinion. ALPAR AI is 'AI Act ready/aligned', not compliant. See Terms of Service for full disclaimer.

methodology.intro: Our proprietary methodology ensures unbiased and transparent rankings.
